description: M6: latency and throughput the gateway adds to one tool call
framing: Single machine: a shared cloud container (KVM guest), not isolated from other tenants, with no CPU pinning or frequency control. Numbers are indicative and vary run to run. Audit fsync cost depends entirely on the disk under the temp dir. Nothing here is compared with any other system. 'added' latency is handle_call time minus the median time of calling the no-op tool directly. 'warm' reuses one token (verify-cache hits), 'cold' uses a token the cache has not seen on every call (signature checked every call); see warm_vs_cold. Stage timings are the public components timed one by one with the same inputs; they need not sum to the pipeline. In-process threads share one GIL, so thread counts above 1 measure contention, not parallel speed-up.
warm_vs_cold: Authority.verify keeps a bounded LRU cache (verify_cache_size entries) of signature-checked parses, keyed by the exact token string. 'warm' reuses one token, so after the first call verify is a cache hit and only the time, revocation and registration checks run: the common case for an agent that makes many calls with one token. 'cold' is the first call with a token: the Ed25519 signature is checked and the claims are parsed. handle_call verifies once (step b) and rechecks the record later (steps d and e) in both modes. The earlier published figure (added p50 1.19 ms, main configuration) was measured before the verify-once change and before the cache existed, when handle_call verified the token string three times; it is not comparable with either number here.

method.gc: left on; gc.collect() before each timed loop
method.cold_tokens: minted with Authority.mint / Authority.exchange before the timed loop; neither puts a token in the verify cache. The pipeline section uses a new token for every call; depth and throughput cycle a pool of cold_pool_size distinct tokens per stream, larger than the cache, so every call still misses. signature_check_count fields are an untimed pass that counts signature checks to confirm each mode. Depth pools are children of one parent, so depth rigs allow that parent 2 * cold_pool_size children (default 64).
method.fsync_off: os.fsync replaced by a no-op for the audit log only; SQLite keeps its own syncs (default rollback journal, synchronous=FULL)
method.clock: real time.time for tokens and policy, time.time_ns for the audit log
method.gateway_options: library defaults (tool runs on the calling thread, no in-flight limit) unless stated; 'server_options' matches caveat.server.build

verify_cold.label: Authority.verify, new token: signature checked, cache miss (step b)

ed25519_signature_only.label: Ed25519 signature check alone (part of a cold verify)

verify_warm.label: Authority.verify, same token again: cache hit, times + revocation + registration (step b)

authorize.label: Authority.authorize(receipt): recheck + grant decide + charge (step d)

budget_charge.label: Store.charge on the delegation path (part of authorize)

http.server: caveat.server.create_app on uvicorn 0.54.0, 1 worker process, 127.0.0.1, HTTP/1.1 keep-alive
http.client: httpx 0.28.1, one httpx.Client (one connection) per client thread, in a separate process from the server
http.token: warm: each client reuses its one token, so the server's verify cache hits after the first call. Cold is not measured over HTTP (it would need thousands of tokens minted through the admin endpoint first).

mcp_proxy.transport: in-process ASGI (httpx2.ASGITransport), no socket; the upstream is examples/mcp_upstream_server.py; MCP SDK client mcp.Client
mcp_proxy.token: warm: one token for every call
mcp_proxy.note: added_p50_us is a difference of medians, not a distribution
